name: The St. Regis Kuala Lumpur
positioning: St. Regis hotel at Kuala Lumpur Sentral, the city's transport hub, with an art collection, seven restaurants and bars, and complimentary butler service
best_for: Travelers who want a base at Kuala Lumpur Sentral, near the Perdana Botanical Gardens and the National Museum
Food and drink lovers interested in Japanese counter dining, wine and whisky
Guests who enjoy art and hotel rituals such as afternoon tea and champagne sabering

facts.text: The hotel is in Kuala Lumpur Sentral, the city's key transportation hub.
The Perdana Botanical Gardens, the National Museum and the House of Parliament are nearby.
The hotel has seven restaurants and bars.
Astor Bar and Decanter holds 650 wine labels in a wine cellar with a gold-tiled domed ceiling.
Tenshin serves Edomae-style tempura omakase, with ingredients flown in from Japan three times a week.
Crystal is a rooftop venue with casual alfresco dining and happy hour cocktails.
Rooms have large seating areas, luggage space and walk-in wardrobes.
Suites can convert into two-bedroom units with adjoining Deluxe Rooms.
Suites have views of either Perdana Botanical Garden or the city skyline.
Iridium Spa looks out over Perdana Botanical Garden and offers LPG Endermologie body-contouring treatments.
The hotel has a rooftop swimming pool.

highlights.text: Afternoon tea in The Drawing Room is served beneath a five-tier crystal chandelier, beside a horse sculpture by Fernando Botero.
The art collection includes Barnaby Hosking's Birds and Butterflies installation, inspired by the Perdana Botanical Gardens, and a butler can guide guests on an art walk.
The Macallan M Room at Astor Bar is Malaysia's first experiential whisky bar.
Taka serves dishes at a 300-year-old Hinoki wood counter.
St. Regis Butler Service is complimentary for all guests, and butlers can bring a chef-prepared picnic to Perdana Botanical Garden.

considerations.text: The hotel does not provide a shuttle service.
The St. Regis Kids Club charges a fee per child per entry.
